newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU court says VAT only payable on discount price.
newsitem.headline: EU court says VAT only payable on discount price.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that VAT is liable only on the discount price of a product, not the full price, a decision that could require the British government to pay back substantial sums.

Interpreting a European Union law on the harmonisation of taxes, the court ruled that because companies only received a discount price for a product on sale, that is what they should pay Value Added Tax on.
"The taxable amount (of a product) is equal to the selling price charged by the manufacturer, less the amount indicated on the voucher and refunded," it ruled.

The case was brought to court by the British tax authorities who wanted a ruling on whether Unilever subsidiary Elida Faberge, a toiletries manufacturer, and retail chain Argos were due repayment of excess VAT.
According to court documents, Unilever asked the British government to repay 883,894 pounds ($1.4 million). Argos asked for 1.4 million pounds.
Some industry reports, however, have suggested that such a ruling could win British companies a payback of as much as 400 million pounds.

"The basic principle of the VAT system is that it is intended to tax only the final consumer. Consequently, the taxable amount serving as a basis for the VAT to be collected by the tax authorities cannot exceed the consideration actually paid by the final consumer," the court said.
